title: arXiv Mathematics — notable papers in the 29 September 2026 batch
ranking_note: Inferred shortlist based on claimed result scope, cross-listing and recency; not an arXiv popularity ranking. Semantic Scholar was rate-limited.

sections.title: Convex counterexamples to the Schiffer and Pompeiu conjectures in dimensions three, four, six, eight, ten and fourteen
sections.abstract: Constructs non-ball convex domains in six specified dimensions with analytic spherical boundaries supporting an overdetermined Helmholtz solution, yielding counterexamples to both conjectures in those dimensions.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims bounded convex non-ball domains in dimensions 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14 for which a nonconstant solution of Δu+u=0 satisfies u=1 and ∇u=0 on the boundary, yielding Schiffer/Pompeiu counterexamples.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Real-analytic spherical boundaries; specific dimensions 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14. Computer-assisted construction with rank-two compact Lie algebra reductions in dimensions 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14, plus an axisymmetric construction in dimension 3.
sections.caveat: Preprint and computer-assisted proof; interval bounds, code and convex-domain reconstruction need independent reproduction and expert review.

sections.title: A proof of the generalized packing-covering conjecture
sections.abstract: Claims a computer-assisted proof, for all linear codes over finite fields and every admissible order, of d_t(C) ≤ 2R_t(C)+2.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the generalized packing-covering inequality for all linear codes, using a parity-check reformulation, length bounds, successive puncturing and exact computer verification of remaining finite cases.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: C is a linear code over any finite field and t is any admissible order; the inequality compares the tth generalized Hamming weight and generalized covering radius.
sections.caveat: Independent checking and reproducibility of the exact finite computation are central; this remains an unreviewed preprint claim.

sections.title: Complete classification of 7-adic Galois images for non-CM elliptic curves over Q
sections.abstract: Claims to settle a conjecture of Furio and Lombardo and thereby complete the classification of 7-adic Galois images for non-CM elliptic curves over Q.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the relevant rational points on a genus-3 modular curve are exactly four specified points, which, combined with cited work, completes the classification.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The main theorem assumes the Jacobian of the curve has Mordell-Weil rank 3; the paper identifies a cited fake 2-Selmer computation as establishing that hypothesis. The argument uses a Mordell-Weil sieve and p-adic heights.
sections.caveat: The rank premise and computational arithmetic need independent verification. The abstract discloses an AI-training process; correctness must be judged from the mathematics and computations.

sections.title: Very sharp distance and range transitions for random walk bridges on Ramanujan graphs
sections.abstract: Finds a bounded critical window in which the maximum distance of a logarithmic-length random-walk bridge changes from order sqrt(log N) to order log N, alongside a two-point limiting law for normalized range.
sections.claimed_result: For vertex-transitive Ramanujan graphs with logarithmic girth, the paper claims a sharp distance transition and a two-point limiting law for normalized range in the same O(1) window.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The graph sequence is vertex-transitive and Ramanujan with logarithmic girth; bridge length is of order log N, where N is graph size.
sections.caveat: Do not generalize to arbitrary expanders or random walks; the graph hypotheses are restrictive and the abstract omits full constants and technical conditions.

sections.title: Qin’s quasimodularity conjecture for Hilbert schemes of points
sections.abstract: Claims the predicted quasimodularity and mixed-weight bound for reduced generating series of tautological-bundle intersection numbers on Hilbert schemes of points, using a trace formula for Nakajima operators.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim Qin’s conjecture for smooth projective complex surfaces with numerically trivial canonical class, including the predicted mixed-weight bound, and give an algorithm for general reduced generating series.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: X is a smooth projective complex surface with numerically trivial canonical class; the series concern tautological bundles and intersection numbers on X^[n].
sections.caveat: The theorem is limited to that surface class. The paper explicitly reports GPT-5.6 Sol assistance and requires independent specialist review.

sections.title: Disproof of the dominating Hadwiger conjecture
sections.abstract: Gives a counterexample to a strengthened Hadwiger-type statement requiring every vertex in each later branch set to connect to each earlier branch set, using a complement of a pseudorandom triangle-free graph.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the dominating Hadwiger conjecture is false, using the complement of a suitably sampled block-geometric triangle-free graph.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Graphs with chromatic number at least t and the stronger dominating K_t-model condition; this does not disprove the original Hadwiger conjecture.
sections.caveat: The abstract says ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra found the disproof and the authors provide an exposition. The argument is a preprint claim requiring independent checking.

sections.title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton–Perelman Proof of the Three-Dimensional Poincaré Conjecture
sections.abstract: Reports a Lean formalization of the smooth three-dimensional Poincaré theorem and Moise smoothing, yielding the topological statement through Ricci flow with surgery and finite-time extinction.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a Lean formalization of the Hamilton–Perelman route, including the smoothing step needed to pass from smooth to topological 3-manifolds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The target is the smooth and topological three-dimensional Poincaré conjecture; the formal route uses Ricci flow with surgery and finite-time extinction.
sections.caveat: The abstract alone does not establish completeness or build status. A Lean project and successful reproducible build are needed; neither was verified here.

sections.title: Partial Regularity of Stable Stationary Harmonic Maps into Compact Lie Groups
sections.abstract: Claims the singular set of every stable stationary harmonic map into a compact Lie group has Hausdorff codimension at least four, and says this bound is sharp.
sections.claimed_result: For stable stationary harmonic maps u:M→G, the singular set has Hausdorff codimension at least four, with sharpness claimed by the author.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: M is compact Riemannian; G is a compact Lie group with a bi-invariant metric; maps are stable and stationary.
sections.caveat: The abstract is very brief and does not expose the regularity argument or sharpness example; exact hypotheses require reading the full paper.
